name: Zendesk
verdict: Zendesk does not let you create the global OAuth client that multi-customer apps need; you build on a local client, then Zendesk reviews and converts it. No review SLA is documented, likely several weeks.
needGuide: Yes — request a sponsored d3v- test account, build on a local client, and ask for global-client conversion only when the app is finished.

auth.detail: Authorization code (+ optional PKCE), refresh_token and client_credentials grants; password grant deprecated. Endpoints are per subdomain (https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/authorizations/new and /oauth/tokens). Code valid 120 s; refresh tokens rotate (old pair invalidated), default 30 days (7-90). Clients created on or after 2026-04-30 default to 30-minute access tokens.

effort.timeToProduction: unknown; likely several weeks (global client review plus Marketplace review, no SLA documented)

approval.gate: Apps serving multiple Zendesk customers with server-side API calls must use a global OAuth client. Zendesk does not let developers create these; you build against a local client, then Zendesk reviews and converts it. Marketplace listing is separate. Per-customer local clients work technically but are not allowed for Marketplace apps (credential-sharing is prohibited).

scopes.why: Broad read/write or resource scopes such as tickets:read, and Zendesk may cap your client's allowed scopes when it approves you.
scopes.summary: Broad scopes (read, write) or resource scopes like tickets:read. Client allowed_scopes caps requests (400 invalid_scope otherwise). Zendesk may set allowed scopes on approval; request only what is needed.

cost: Free to build and list; sponsored test account is free; payment setup only if the app is paid
prerequisites: Account and owner: Admin (or agent with Manage APIs permission) on the test subdomain to create the client; a company-owned Marketplace portal login with a registered organization and profile.

Where you register: Local client: Admin Center → Apps and integrations → APIs → OAuth clients → Add OAuth client (identifier must start with zdg-). Global client: Marketplace portal (apps.zendesk.com) → Global OAuth → Request new OAuth.
Cost: Free to build and list; sponsored test account is free; payment setup only if the app is paid

registerAt.path: Local client: Admin Center → Apps and integrations → APIs → OAuth clients → Add OAuth client (identifier must start with zdg-). Global client: Marketplace portal (apps.zendesk.com) → Global OAuth → Request new OAuth.

steps.do: Request a sponsored Zendesk test account (subdomain prefix d3v-) via the Marketplace developer docs
Create local OAuth client: Admin Center → Apps and integrations → APIs → OAuth clients; identifier zdg-yourapp, fill every field, confidential kind, redirect URIs, scopes
Implement authorization code flow with PKCE per customer subdomain; store rotating refresh tokens and handle 401 by refresh
Test end-to-end against the sponsored account with narrow scopes (e.g. tickets:read, tickets:write)
Save the client secret and identifier, then apps.zendesk.com → Global OAuth → Request new OAuth with d3v- subdomain and the matching zdg- id
Wait for approval email/ticket; update production config; contact Zendesk Support (Option 2, mention global oauth) for later scope changes
Register organization, create Marketplace profile, and submit listing with data-access disclosure

roles.team: Admin (or agent with Manage APIs permission) on the test subdomain to create the client; a company-owned Marketplace portal login with a registered organization and profile.
roles.console: Marketplace org/profile: none documented for collaborators. Local clients: admins and agents with Manage APIs can create, update, delete and regenerate the secret. Only Zendesk's Marketplace Operations Team can edit a global client afterwards.
roles.customer: Zendesk user who authorizes at /oauth/authorizations/new; the token inherits that user's role and the client's allowed scopes. Plan must be Suite or Support Team/Professional/Enterprise (OAuth clients per help article). Install of Marketplace apps likely needs an admin.

testing: Request a sponsored test account (Marketplace docs).
The global-client request requires a subdomain with the d3v- prefix.
Build with a local client first.
Sell uses a different mechanism (Multi-User Application).

blockers.fix: Request it only when the app is finished, with the production zdg- identifier already in use.

blockers.problem: You lose access to the local client admin page after conversion

blockers.fix: Collect the customer subdomain before redirecting.
Persist the new pair atomically or the connection breaks.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth/PKCE code and refresh handling, run test API calls, draft the global-OAuth request justification, scope rationale and Marketplace listing copy, and call the OAuth clients API.
automation.humanMust: Sign in to the Marketplace portal, submit the global OAuth form, register the organization, accept partner/legal terms, and handle any payment setup.

uncertain: Review duration for global clients and Marketplace listings; exact admin role for global-client submission; whether a global client strictly requires a Marketplace listing (docs say only to request it when the app is ready).
Zendesk OAuth clients reference pages for global clients returned fetch errors.
